observation: The review says hook coverage gaps have no re-anchor beyond TTL/focus and proposes prompt return as ending evidence.
claimed_consequence: Missed transitions can leave stale attention, and prompt evidence is proposed as a cheaper end signal.
proposed_remedy: Use shell prompt observations, treating Ctrl-Z as a recoverable false positive.

evidence.observed: prompt_return validates the inherited claim and writes an activity-clear watermark, not an end record.
Passed; child records survive, no end.json is created and newer work reactivates lead activity.
Current vendor documentation distinguishes user interruption from a normal Stop callback.

reachability_basis: A missed hook, suspended/background process, or prompt-return ordering is required; current prompt handling is a limited recovery signal.
invariant: A shell prompt observation must not assert provider-session termination, because suspension, background execution and nested shells can also return a prompt.
smallest_complete_fix: Retain current lead-only prompt clear and its stated limitations; document that an in-agent interrupt can still wait for TTL.
risk_if_deferred: If the limits are omitted, downstream tools can confuse quiet attention with ended work.
risk_if_fixed_now: Writing end.json on prompt return could make suspended/background sessions eligible for ending/retention semantics.
action: Document that the Rust port already uses prompt return as lead-activity clear, not binding end. Do not adopt the stronger end inference.
disproof: Current prompt_return writes activity-clear.json only; its test asserts no end.json and no agents-clear.json.
draft_response: Prompt recovery already exists in Rust with weaker, safer semantics. It clears lead attention; it does not prove that the agent ended.

observation: The first publication request fires before all panes attach and is latched on spawn.
claimed_consequence: Later panes stay unpublished and attention remains missing after reconnect.
proposed_remedy: Retry with backoff until publication is observed, rather than treating spawn as success.

evidence.observed: Retry state is per realm with per-window observations; resolution and closed windows are reconciled explicitly.
Fresh PWD-corrected run passed all 111 cases, including late/unpublished panes, alternating windows, window closure and failed-spawn retry.

reachability_basis: The earlier condition was checked against the current Rust-era code; the cited implementation or test disproves it as a remaining defect.
invariant: Unpublished panes must keep recovery eligible until current observations resolve them, without one window cancelling another window's work.
risk_if_deferred: No deferral: the cited one-shot implementation was replaced.
risk_if_fixed_now: Reapplying the old repair could disturb working multi-window retry ownership.
action: Reject as a current defect; retain the Rust-era Lua retry implementation and tests.
disproof: Current runtime uses 2/5/10/30-second retries, stable-pane observations, per-window ownership and token cancellation rather than the old one-shot latch.
draft_response: Fixed by the Rust-era Lua rewrite. The fresh retry cases pass; a full live GUI reattach rehearsal was not repeated in this triage.

claimed_consequence: Republishing fails before reading any pane.
proposed_remedy: Use WezTerm's executable directory and explicit executable fallbacks.

Passed in the current Rust suite; unsafe writable fallback paths are also tested.
Installed WezTerm protocol/formatter smoke passed with 35 parser and 10 eligibility rows.

reachability_basis: The earlier condition was checked against the current Rust-era code; the cited implementation or test disproves it as a remaining defect.

risk_if_deferred: The missing-path mechanism has a current implementation and regression tests.

action: Reject as a current defect; retain the current executable resolver and GUI PATH handoff.
disproof: Lua prepends wezterm.executable_dir. Rust supports configured and trusted application-path fallbacks.
draft_response: Fixed in current code. Empty-PATH resolution passes; the smoke is not a claim that every Dock launch was exercised.

observation: The review proposes minting a launch in SessionStart without inherited launch identity and relying on /dev/tty, binding hashes and monotonic order.
claimed_consequence: It would remove the zsh setup problem while purportedly preserving stale-callback protection.
proposed_remedy: Enable SessionStart self-claim after verifying /dev/tty reachability.

evidence.observed: The resolver first checks inherited launch, then a tty-matching stored claim; minting requires an explicit gate.
Fresh controlled-pty test passed its assertion that the macOS /dev/tty alias cannot establish pane identity.
Fresh test passed for both stand-in enabled and default-disabled paths.
Current Claude command-hook contract runs hooks in a separate session without a controlling terminal. This is vendor documentation, not a paid provider contact test.

reachability_basis: A fresh launch without an inherited or usable stored claim reaches the default-disabled self-claim gate.
invariant: Before automatic lifecycle activation, every hook must resolve the exact process generation and pane; opening a terminal alias or hashing a session ID is not sufficient ownership evidence.
smallest_complete_fix: Verify a provider-supported pane/process-generation correlation mechanism, including later callbacks and same-session resume, before enabling the gated path.
risk_if_deferred: Ordinary unclaimed provider launches remain outside v2, but the current gate prevents an unsupported automatic attribution path.
risk_if_fixed_now: Enabling it from a synthetic tty proof can misattribute generations or fail under the provider's real process-spawn contract.
action: Keep WEZTERM_ATTENTION_ENABLE_SELF_CLAIM disabled by default. Follow-up scope and activation block are recorded in followups.md#automatic-launch-correlation.
disproof: The current macOS test opens /dev/tty but rejects its identity; current Claude documentation states command hooks have no controlling terminal. A newer observation also cannot identify which generation emitted an otherwise identical same-session callback.
draft_response: The launch gap is real, but route A is not a complete production design. The Rust implementation correctly keeps it gated; do not enable it based only on the old recommendation.

observation: The proposed Rust design would retire the executed manifest and rely on separately maintained contract copies.
claimed_consequence: Rust/Lua meanings could diverge despite published schemas.
proposed_remedy: Embed the manifest, execute its constraints and assert parity with fixtures/typed representations.

evidence.observed: The embedded manifest is parsed and used by record validation; it is not passive documentation.
All passed in the current Rust suite.

risk_if_fixed_now: Adding duplicate constants solely to compare them would create another representation to maintain.
action: Reject the stale retirement claim. Preserve manifest execution and existing parity tests; assess any future typed mirror when it is introduced.
disproof: protocol.rs uses include_str!, typed Manifest/FieldType parsing, and runtime limits/enums. Byte parity, unknown-field-type rejection and shared corpus tests pass.
draft_response: Fixed by the Rust port. Most limits/enums are read from the manifest, so a test of nonexistent duplicate constants is not itself a missing feature.

observation: The review cites an Orca workaround that prints an empty JSON object because empty permission-hook stdout allegedly fails closed.
claimed_consequence: A silent attention hook could change permission behavior on the installed provider.
proposed_remedy: Verify an empty object response against the installed Claude version before adopting it.

evidence.observed: The current hook dispatch is quiet on success and writes diagnostics to stderr.
Orca has a conditional neutral-JSON fallback; that alone does not establish this installed provider's behavior.

A single authorized Claude 2.1.266 interaction invoked an exit-0, zero-stdout PermissionRequest hook, then displayed the normal permission prompt. The command was refused and its target file remained absent.
Current docs distinguish non-interactive denial when no decision is available from a hook parse failure. An empty object itself supplies no allow/deny decision.

reachability_basis: The installed interactive provider reached a Bash PermissionRequest with the same quiet-success hook shape and preserved the normal permission decision UI.
invariant: An observational attention hook must not grant, deny or unexpectedly block a provider permission decision.
risk_if_deferred: The installed-provider probe establishes no regression in the existing quiet hook contract.
risk_if_fixed_now: A blanket stdout change could alter other event contracts and would be an unverified compatibility workaround.
action: Reject the blanket neutral-JSON workaround; retain zero stdout for the observational PermissionRequest hook.
disproof: Claude 2.1.266 invoked the exit-0, zero-stdout hook and then showed its normal permission prompt without a parse error or implicit decision.
draft_response: Refuted on the installed provider. Empty successful stdout preserves the normal permission prompt; no {} workaround is needed.

claimed_consequence: Debug or progress output could contaminate the provider's context.

action: Retain the current quiet-success contract and stdout/stderr tests; no implementation change.
draft_response: Confirmed and already protected. No new quiet-output implementation is needed.

observation: Focus acknowledges notify by default even if the provider is still waiting.
claimed_consequence: A user can leave the pane after viewing a permission prompt and no longer see its alert.
proposed_remedy: Decide whether notify clears on focus or only after later provider activity.

evidence.observed: Default acknowledged types include stop and notify; opts.auto_clear can change the set.
An exact acknowledgement is written without deleting the provider activity record.
Fresh 111-case suite passed focus/exact-ack and configured acknowledgement behavior.

reachability_basis: The inspected behavior is reachable through the documented configuration, normal callback, reader or explicit CLI path.
invariant: Changing acknowledgement policy must preserve the distinction between viewed notification, outstanding provider wait and ended work.
smallest_complete_fix: Choose alert policy explicitly; the existing auto_clear option can exclude notify. Distinguishing permission waits from every other notify may need a separate fact.
risk_if_deferred: Current shipped focus behavior remains; some unanswered prompts can be visually quiet.
risk_if_fixed_now: A blanket change affects manual/general notifications as well as permission prompts and can create persistent alerts.
action: Record as a user-policy decision, not an accepted runtime bug. Keep the existing default until the user chooses; do not rewrite every notify as blocked.
draft_response: Confirmed behavior, but not a settled defect. The trade-off is notification policy; existing configuration already supports stop-only acknowledgement.

observation: Persisted ordering uses CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW, not a per-process Instant baseline.

Passed in the fresh real-hook subprocess test.

draft_response: Already implemented. Keep the per-boot clock-coordinate and incarnation-scope distinction explicit.

observation: The current prescribed Bun test command fails at writer dispatch and subsequent queued cases; the isolated Node dispatch smoke cannot read its expected calls log.

evidence.observed: The exact Bun command from tests/gate.sh finished with 23 passed, 7 failed across 30 tests; first v2 dispatch timed out at 5000 ms.
The isolated Node smoke reported ENOENT for its generated writer calls.log. A focused Bun v2-dispatch case also timed out.

A generated script executed through /bin/sh completed; one direct Node script execution timed out. The stable repository shim completed --help. These controls narrow the investigation but do not prove the cause.
A stable native executable returning nonzero was correctly classified by the Pi adapter, with a warning and no v1 fallback file.

reachability_basis: The prescribed repository Bun test command reproduced the failure, not only the more restricted env -i runs. Impact on actual provider-hosted execution is not yet established.

smallest_complete_fix: Diagnose the generated-writer execution boundary under the supported Node/Bun environment and restore the dispatch/failure proofs without weakening no-downgrade, queue ordering or shutdown contracts.
risk_if_deferred: The current full gate is not green and Pi delivery could be misreported as verified. Actual provider impact remains unknown.
risk_if_fixed_now: A blind timeout increase or queue rewrite could mask a fixture/host execution problem; root cause must precede any patch.
action: Accept the verification failure for diagnosis before fresh Pi/full-gate certification. No product or test fix was applied. Follow-up evidence is recorded in followups.md#pi-dispatch-verification.
